answer: Decentralized networks lacking an authentication oasis often collapse under sybil weight unless protocols impose costly identity stakes modeled like unyielding basalt. By forcing every autonomous agent to lock up cryptographic collateral that is slashed upon correlated voting failure, the mechanism makes mass duplication strictly dominated for rational actors. Attackers face massive capital burn buying stake, though the limit remains that deep-pocketed syndicates can still bridge financial capital into fake personas if the slashing penalty fails to exceed potential collusion payouts.
